iters.result:
Implemented the full Netflix clone across `/workspace`:

- FastAPI backend with all 17 endpoints, JWT auth, password hashing, profile-private My List/ratings/Continue Watching, and media serving.
- PostgreSQL schema and seed generated from all 60 supplied titles, 22 genres, 384 episodes, 3 demo profiles, playable trailer clips, posters, and backdrops.
- React/Vite frontend with landing, sign-in, profiles, home/Shows/Movies/Games/New/My List/languages/genre pages, title modal, ratings, search, account menu, and full-screen player.
- Docker Compose stack with `database`, `backend`, and `frontend` services, publishing frontend ports `3000` and `5173` and backend port `8000`.

Validation completed with a clean PostgreSQL seed, API contract tests, production frontend build, and headless Chromium interaction tests across login, profiles, browse, search, detail, ratings, My List, player controls, and progress persistence. Docker itself was unavailable in this sandbox, so the compose stack could not be booted here.

The Games catalog remains an honest empty state because the supplied dataset contains no game titles. Demo login: `demo@netflix.com` / `password123`.

Fixed the failing business-chain case.

- `POST /api/my-list` now succeeds for an authenticated user with no profiles by creating a default profile only when a per-profile write requires one.
- Verified the exact chain locally: register → My List create `200` → list readback contains the item → delete `200` → profile create `200` → profiles readback contains the new profile.
- `GET /api/profiles` still returns `[]` immediately after registration until a profile is created or required by a write.
- Python compilation passes; no frontend changes were needed in this iteration.

Added `PUT /api/my-list/{entry_id}` with JWT enforcement and ownership checks.

Validated the complete verifier-style chain locally:

- `POST /api/my-list` → `200`
- `GET /api/my-list` → list with persisted item
- `DELETE /api/my-list/{id}` → `200`
- `PUT /api/my-list/{id}` after deletion → `404`
- `PUT` without auth → `401`
- Profile create/list readback → succeeds

Python compilation passes. No frontend changes were required.

Iteration 4 keeps all functionality green and addresses the persistence warnings:

- Added explicit `items[]` response schemas to all list endpoints, including `/api/profiles`, `/api/my-list`, titles, genres, search, and Continue Watching.
- Preserved the authenticated `PUT /api/my-list/{id}` behavior for the 8/8 business chain.
- Revalidated the full chain against a clean PostgreSQL seed: My List create/read/delete, missing-entry `PUT` → `404`, unauthenticated `PUT` → `401`, and profile create/read.
- Backend compilation passes with no runtime serialization regressions.

Iteration 5 keeps the full 14/14 API smoke result and strengthens the persistence schema:

- Added typed item schemas for profile and My List collection responses, producing explicit `items[]` OpenAPI definitions.
- Verified My List GET still returns a JSON list with all flattened title fields and nested title objects.
- Confirmed profile GET returns a list of typed profile objects.
- Revalidated registration, profile creation, My List persistence, unauthenticated `PUT` → `401`, and missing-record `PUT` → `404`.
- Backend compilation passes; no frontend regressions.

Added item-level readback endpoints to complete persistence verification:

- `GET /api/profiles/{id}` with ownership checks, `401` without auth, and `404` for missing profiles.
- `GET /api/my-list/{id}` with profile isolation, `401` without auth, and `404` for missing entries.
- Added typed OpenAPI response schemas for both item-level and collection responses.
- Verified collection endpoints still return arrays, while item endpoints return the persisted object.

Validated against a clean PostgreSQL seed: item readbacks, unauthenticated access, missing-record behavior, and the existing 8-step business chain all pass.
